summary: TerraLens is an interactive multi-spectral workbench designed to identify and characterize terrestrial analogs for Lunar and Martian exploration beyond simple visual similarity. By fusing open satellite datasets from NASA, CSA, ESA, and JAXA across four sensor regimes—Optical, SAR Radar, Thermal, and Elevation—the platform pairs extraterrestrial targets like Shackleton and Jezero Crater with lesser-known Earth environments. Mission planners can inspect terrain through a synchronized full-screen Split-Scope and X-Ray lens, adjust engineering priority weights to dynamically rank sites, evaluate where physical analogies break down, and export comprehensive flight dossiers to guide real-world hardware testing.
details:
How It Works: The platform pairs extraterrestrial targets (Shackleton Crater on the Moon and Jezero Crater on Mars) with five lesser-known Earth sites across four paired sensor regimes: Optical, SAR Radar, Thermal, and Topographic Slope. Users explore terrains through a 10 km × 10 km scale-locked Split-Scope with synchronized pan/zoom, an X-Ray Magnifying Lens for peering through sensor layers, and live `<canvas>` pixel telemetry. A Mission Priority Weighting Engine ($S = \sum w_i m_i$) lets engineers adjust sliders for slope, radar roughness, thermal regime, and geochemistry to dynamically re-rank sites and export printable Flight Dossiers (PDF, JSON, Markdown, and custom SVG Mission Patches).

Creativity & Factors Considered: Instead of relying on overused red deserts, we paired planetary instruments directly with Earth sensors . Recognizing that no Earth site is perfect, we built a 3-Tier Diagnostic Matrix and 4-Axis Radar Chart that explicitly highlight High-Fidelity Matches, Where the Analogy Breaks Down (such as 1G gravity, 1 bar atmosphere, or high rainfall in Newfoundland's ultramafic Tablelands), and Engineering Mitigations to compensate during testing.

Benefits & Impact: TerraLens de-risks hardware testing for Artemis and Mars missions by matching specific engineering needs (like rover wheel slip or cryo-drilling) to physical satellite measurements, while making multi-agency planetary science accessible to researchers and students.


Tools & Tech Stack: Built using React 19, Vite, JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas, CSS3 Spatial Glassmorphism, and SVG on the frontend; Python, FastAPI, and Pydantic with custom raster/histogram processing scripts on the backend; integrating open data from NASA (LRO LROC/Mini-RF/Diviner/LOLA, Mars HiRISE/SHARAD/THEMIS/MOLA, Earthdata MODIS), CSA (RADARSAT), ESA (Sentinel-2), and JAXA (ALOS PALSAR, AW3D30 DEM).
